correctness.rationale: For r>=4, all allocations a=0,1,2,3 leave a clique follower. Eigenmode decomposition of the actual grounded Laplacian yields the exact rational J_a, including the v=0 boundary by cancellation. Signs of explicit algebraic differences handle m=3,4,5,6; for m>=7 both competing numerators have positive-coefficient representations after P=r-4,Q=m-7, and J2-J3 has sign r-6. These cover all integer parameters and establish all ties. The embedded checker independently verifies 24 algebraic identities, 45,746 exact parameter comparisons and 140 independently assembled dense inverse traces; finite tests only corroborate the proof.

originality.rationale: The general objective and general m-leader joint centrality are explicitly credited to Fitch--Leonard, with further resistance formulations credited to Patterson--Yi--Zhang. Accessible adjacent exact results concern two leaders on weighted split networks or three leaders on bipartite networks. Neither implies the specific three-leader complete-split optimizer phase table with critical clique counts 20,10,6 and full ties. Targeted published mathematical-record and literature searches did not reveal a stronger exact theorem; meaningful residual coverage uncertainty is documented.
residual_risks: The available mathematical-record searches returned many distant topics; relevant unindexed or differently named leader-selection literature may exist.
Neither source inspection is an exhaustive line-by-line review of every available paper, and no global uniqueness conclusion follows from a search.
General joint-centrality identities theoretically permit derivation of specialized graph classes; publication of this exact phase table outside indexed sources remains possible.
No independent mathematical validation has been performed.

value.rationale: This is a natural complete classification for core/periphery consensus design with exactly three costly direct measurements. It shows nontrivial leader relocation when core and peripheral populations vary, including three distinct sharp integer transition scales and a genuine three-way tie at (r,m)=(6,6). Every optimum and its multiplicity are determined, distinguishing network-structure sensitivity from a routine objective evaluation.
